post.caption: The Golden Spike carried the wrong date. A San Francisco businessman named David Hewes had it made for the end of the first transcontinental railroad. It is 17.6 karat gold and weighs about 14 ounces. The words The Last Spike are engraved on its head. One side says the railroad was completed on May 8, 1869, but the ceremony at Promontory Summit was two days later. The railroad's president swung at the spike and missed. A telegraph operator still sent the word done. The gold spike was only tapped, then replaced with iron. Its twin, kept in Sacramento, says May 10, 1869.
